blocks.text: A good healthcheck is cheap, local, fast, and tests what clients actually use; it runs inside the container on every interval, forever.

blocks.code:
# Postgres: TCP, not the socket
test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5432 -U $${POSTGRES_USER} -d $${POSTGRES_DB}"]
# Qdrant: minimal image may lack curl → TCP probe
test: ["CMD-SHELL", "bash -c ':> /dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/6333' || exit 1"]
# FastAPI: use the Python you ship
test: ["CMD", "python", "-c", "import urllib.request,sys; sys.exit(0 if urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/readyz',timeout=2).status==200 else 1)"]

items: Postgres `-h 127.0.0.1`: during first init the temporary server is socket-only, so a socket check can report ready before TCP clients can connect.
Qdrant exposes `/healthz`, `/livez`, `/readyz` on 6333; check which tools the image has.
API: `/healthz` shallow liveness; `/readyz` cheap dependency check (`SELECT 1`).

rows: No LLM calls or vector searches

blocks.text: Q: "What makes a good healthcheck?" A: "It's cheap, local and tests the client path: pg_isready over TCP for Postgres, a readiness endpoint that does SELECT 1 for the API, with a start_period covering cold start. It never calls paid or slow external services."
